newsitem.title: GERMANY: Air China offers Germany/N Korea cargo.
newsitem.headline: Air China offers Germany/N Korea cargo.

text.p: Chinese National carrier Air China is offering air cargo transport from Germany to North Korea and Mongolia via Beijing, its German agent said.
Frank Wortmann, managing director of the airline's Germany cargo sales agent Penta Shipping GmbH, said Pyongyang and the Mongolian capital Ulan Bator were now available as transhipment destinations.
"There are a few small consignments, mostly documents," he told Reuters in an interview.
The rate per kg for a 100kg shipment to Pyongyang is 8.50 marks and to Ulan Bator is 6.30 marks, he said.
Air China flies weekly with a McDonnell Douglas MD-82 passenger aircraft from Beijing to the North Korean capital, Wortmann said.
Both destinations could also be reached from Beijing by road or rail freight transport, he added.
Penta Shipping has re-structured rates for through delivery by air or land from Beijing to the Chinese provinces into four groups according to distance from the capital, Wortmann said.
The company has six offices in China, including two each in Beijing and Shanghai, and seven handling agents at major Chinese airports.
Penta Shipping was appointed Air China cargo sales agent from September 1995 after a new agreement between the airline and Lufthansa Cargo AG, the previous sales agent, Wortmann said.

Penta Shipping is 50 percent owned by state-owned China Ocean Shipping (Group) Co, with the remaining stake held by two private Danish investors. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
